title: The bootstrap file of store@
description: Bootstrap is the bootstrap file. store@ reads all of it; key@ reads the publishers and nothing else.

$schema.description: The identifier of this schema, for editors.

boundary.description: The boundary this store@ serves. Every address it handles begins with it. Lower-case kebab-case, 1 to 32 characters, starting with a letter.

start_timeout.description: How long store@ waits at start for each driver to pass its check and for the config source to answer: a duration written with a unit, such as 30s or 2m. The default is 30s.

config_source.description: The destination of the config class.

secret_source.description: The destination of the secret class.

durable.description: The destination of the durable class.

temp.description: The destination of the temp class.

publishers.description: The pinned public keys that sign config. At least one: a list that verifies nothing could never load config.

BootstrapDestination.description: BootstrapDestination names the driver behind one of store@'s four ports and the Unix socket where store@ reaches it.

driver.description: The driver of the port. The values are those of the installation, which store@ checks against the drivers it knows for the port.

socket.description: The absolute path of the driver's Unix socket.

BootstrapPublisher.description: BootstrapPublisher is a public key that may sign config documents.

kid.description: The key's name, unique in the list. Lower-case kebab-case, 1 to 32 characters, starting with a letter.

public_key.description: The key as a PEM PUBLIC KEY (SubjectPublicKeyInfo), an EC P-384 key.

spki_sha384.description: The pin: the SHA-384 of the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, in lower-case hex.

co_signs.description: The kinds whose documents need this key's signature as well as a publisher's that has no co_signs.
